sanskrit: atha nārāyaṇāḥ kruddhā vividhāyudhapāṇayaḥ chādayantaḥ śaravrātaiḥ parivavrur dhanaṃjayam
english: Then the Nārāyaṇa troops, enraged and bearing weapons of every kind, blanketing him with showers of arrows, surrounded Dhanaṃjaya on all sides.

sanskrit: adṛśyaṃ ca muhūrtena cakrus te bharatarṣabha kṛṣṇena sahitaṃ yuddhe kuntīputraṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: And in a moment, O bull of the Bhāratas, they made Dhanaṃjaya, the son of Kuntī, together with Kṛṣṇa, invisible in the battle.

sanskrit: kruddhas tu phalgunaḥ saṃkhye dviguṇīkṛtavikramaḥ gāṇḍīvam upasaṃmṛjya tūrṇaṃ jagrāha saṃyuge
english: But Phalguna, enraged in the fray, his prowess redoubled, stroked the Gāṇḍīva and swiftly took it up in the combat.

sanskrit: baddhvā ca bhṛkuṭīṃ vaktre krodhasya pratilakṣaṇam devadattaṃ mahāśaṅkhaṃ pūrayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Knitting his brow upon his face, the very mark of wrath, the Pāṇḍava filled with breath the great conch Devadatta.

sanskrit: athāstram arisaṃghaghnaṃ tvāṣṭram abhyasyad arjunaḥ tato rūpasahasrāṇi prādurāsan pṛthak pṛthak
english: Then Arjuna loosed the weapon of Tvaṣṭṛ, slayer of hosts of foes, and at once thousands of forms appeared, each one distinct.

sanskrit: ātmanaḥ pratirūpais tair nānārūpair vimohitāḥ anyonyam arjunaṃ matvā svam ātmānaṃ ca jaghnire
english: Deluded by those counterfeit likenesses of him, of manifold shapes, they took one another for Arjuna and slew their very own selves.

sanskrit: ayam arjuno 'yaṃ govinda imau yādavapāṇḍavau iti bruvāṇāḥ saṃmūḍhā jaghnur anyonyam āhave
english: "Here is Arjuna! Here is Govinda! Here are the Yādava and the Pāṇḍava!"—so crying, bewildered, they slew one another in the battle.

sanskrit: mohitāḥ paramāstreṇa kṣayaṃ jagmuḥ parasparam aśobhanta raṇe yodhāḥ puṣpitā iva kiṃśukāḥ
english: Deluded by the supreme weapon, they wrought one another's destruction; the warriors gleamed upon the field like kiṃśuka trees in flower.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasrāṇi tair vimuktāni bhasmasāt kṛtvā tad astraṃ tān vīrān anayad yamasādanam
english: Then that weapon, reducing to ashes the thousands of arrows loosed by them, conducted those heroes to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: atha prahasya bībhatsur lalitthān mālavān api mācellakāṃs trigartāṃś ca yaudheyāṃś cārdayac charaiḥ
english: Then Bībhatsu, laughing, tormented with his arrows the Lalitthas and the Mālavas, the Mācellakas, the Trigartas, and the Yaudheyas.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā vīreṇa kṣatriyāḥ kālacoditāḥ vyasṛjañ śaravarṣāṇi pārthe nānāvidhāni ca
english: Those Kṣatriyas, slaughtered by the hero and driven on by fate, poured upon Pārtha showers of arrows of every kind.

sanskrit: tato naivārjunas tatra na ratho na ca keśavaḥ pratyadṛśyata ghoreṇa śaravarṣeṇa saṃvṛtaḥ
english: Then neither Arjuna nor the chariot nor Keśava could there be seen, shrouded by that dreadful rain of arrows.

sanskrit: tatas te labdhalakṣyatvād anyonyam abhicukruśuḥ hatau kṛṣṇāv iti prītā vāsāṃsy ādudhuvus tadā
english: Then, believing they had found their mark, they shouted to one another in joy, "The two Kṛṣṇas are slain!"—and shook out their garments.

sanskrit: bherīmṛdaṅgaśaṅkhāṃś ca dadhmur vīrāḥ sahasraśaḥ siṃhanādaravāṃś cogrāṃś cakrire tatra māriṣa
english: The warriors by the thousand sounded kettledrums, tabors, and conches, and there, O venerable one, they raised fierce roars like the roaring of lions.

sanskrit: tataḥ prasiṣvide kṛṣṇaḥ khinnaś cārjunam abravīt kvāsi pārtha na paśye tvāṃ kaccij jīvasi śatruhan
english: Then Kṛṣṇa broke into sweat, and weary he said to Arjuna: "Where are you, Pārtha? I do not see you—do you yet live, O slayer of foes?"

sanskrit: tasya taṃ mānuṣaṃ bhāvaṃ bhāvajño ''jñāya pāṇḍavaḥ vāyavyāstreṇa tair astāṃ śaravṛṣṭim apāharat
english: Reading that mortal feeling in him, the Pāṇḍava, who knew all hearts, swept away with the weapon of Vāyu the rain of arrows they had loosed.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃśaptakavrātān sāśvadviparathāyudhān uvāha bhagavān vāyuḥ śuṣkaparṇacayān iva
english: Then the lord Vāyu bore off the hosts of the Saṃśaptakas, with their horses, elephants, chariots, and weapons, as if they were heaps of dry leaves.

sanskrit: uhyamānās tu te rājan bahv aśobhanta vāyunā praḍīnāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ kāle vṛkṣebhya iva māriṣa
english: Borne aloft by the wind, O king, they made a strange spectacle, O venerable one, like birds flying up from the trees in their season.

sanskrit: tāṃs tathā vyākulīkṛtya tvaramāṇo dhanaṃjayaḥ jaghāna niśitair bāṇaiḥ sahasrāṇi śatāni ca
english: Having thus thrown them into confusion, Dhanaṃjaya in haste slew with his whetted arrows hundreds and thousands of them.

sanskrit: śirāṃsi bhallair aharad bāhūn api ca sāyudhān hastihastopamāṃś corūñ śarair urvyām apātayat
english: With broad-headed shafts he struck off heads and arms still grasping their weapons, and with his arrows he felled to the earth thighs like the trunks of elephants.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhacchinnān vicaraṇān vimastiṣkekṣaṇāṅgulīn nānāṅgāvayavair hīnāṃś cakārārīn dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Dhanaṃjaya made his foes broken-backed and legless, their brains, eyes, and fingers shorn away, robbed of their various limbs and members.

sanskrit: gandharvanagarākārān vidhivat kalpitān rathān śarair viśakalīkurvaṃś cakre vyaśvarathadvipān
english: Shattering with his arrows the chariots, duly fashioned and resembling the cities of the Gandharvas, he left them stripped of horses, chariots, and elephants.

sanskrit: muṇḍatālavanānīva tatra tatra cakāśire chinnadhvajarathavrātāḥ ke cit ke cit kva cit kva cit
english: Here and there shone the throngs of chariots with banners cut away, like groves of headless palms—some here, some there, in this place and in that.

sanskrit: sottarāyudhino nāgāḥ sapatākāṅkuśāyudhāḥ petuḥ śakrāśanihatā drumavanta ivācalāḥ
english: Elephants with their upper weapons, with banners, goads, and arms, fell like wooded mountains struck by the thunderbolt of Śakra.

sanskrit: cāmarāpīḍakavacāḥ srastāntranayanāsavaḥ sārohās turagāḥ petuḥ pārthabāṇahatāḥ kṣitau
english: Horses with chowries, head-ornaments, and armor, their entrails, eyes, and breath slipping from them, fell to the ground with their riders, struck down by Pārtha's arrows.

sanskrit: vipraviddhāsinakharāś chinnavarmarṣṭiśaktayaḥ pattayaś chinnavarmāṇaḥ kṛpaṇaṃ śerate hatāḥ
english: Their swords and daggers flung aside, their armor, lances, and spears hewn through, the foot-soldiers with sundered mail lay slain in pitiful array.

sanskrit: tair hatair hanyamānaiś ca patadbhiḥ patitair api bhramadbhir niṣṭanadbhiś ca ghoram āyodhanaṃ babhau
english: With the slain and the dying, with those falling and those fallen, with those reeling about and those groaning aloud, the battlefield grew terrible to behold.

sanskrit: rajaś ca mahad udbhūtaṃ śāntaṃ rudhiravṛṣṭibhiḥ mahī cāpy abhavad durgā kabandhaśatasaṃkulā
english: The great cloud of dust that had risen was laid to rest by the showers of blood, and the earth, thronged with hundreds of headless trunks, became impassable.

sanskrit: tad babhau raudrabībhatsaṃ bībhatsor yānam āhave ākrīḍa iva rudrasya ghnataḥ kālātyaye paśūn
english: That course of Bībhatsu in the battle, fierce and ghastly, shone like the sporting-ground of Rudra slaughtering his creatures at the end of an age.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ pārthena vyākulāśvarathadvipāḥ tam evābhimukhāḥ kṣīṇāḥ śakrasyātithitāṃ gatāḥ
english: Slaughtered by Pārtha, their horses, chariots, and elephants thrown into disorder, they, dwindling away yet still facing him, became the guests of Śakra.

sanskrit: sā bhūmir bharataśreṣṭha nihatais tair mahārathaiḥ āstīrṇā saṃbabhau sarvā pretībhūtaiḥ samantataḥ
english: That ground, O best of the Bhāratas, strewn all over with those slain great chariot-warriors turned into corpses, presented a fearful sight on every side.

sanskrit: etasminn antare caiva pramatte savyasācini vyūḍhānīkas tato droṇo yudhiṣṭhiram upādravat
english: Meanwhile, while Savyasācin was thus occupied, Droṇa, his ranks arrayed in battle order, rushed upon Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: taṃ pratyagṛhṇaṃs tvaritā vyūḍhānīkāḥ prahāriṇaḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ parīpsantas tadāsīt tumulaṃ mahat
english: Swiftly the warriors with their ordered ranks received him, seeking to shield Yudhiṣṭhira; and then there arose a great tumult.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca pariṇāmya niśāṃ tāṃ tu bhāradvājo mahārathaḥ bahūktvā ca tato rājan rājānaṃ ca suyodhanam
english: Saṃjaya said: When the great chariot-warrior, the son of Bharadvāja, had passed that night, and had spoken much, O king, to King Suyodhana,

sanskrit: vidhāya yogaṃ pārthena saṃśaptakagaṇaiḥ saha niṣkrānte ca raṇāt pārthe saṃśaptakavadhaṃ prati
english: having arranged the engagement of Pārtha with the bands of the Saṃśaptakas, and when Pārtha had withdrawn from the field toward the slaying of the Saṃśaptakas,

sanskrit: vyūḍhānīkas tato droṇaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahācamūm abhyayād bharataśreṣṭha dharmarājajighṛkṣayā
english: then Droṇa, his army arrayed for battle, advanced, O best of the Bhāratas, against the great host of the Pāṇḍavas, seeking to seize the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: vyūhaṃ dṛṣṭvā suparṇaṃ tu bhāradvājakṛtaṃ tadā vyūhena maṇḍalārdhena pratyavyūhad yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Beholding then the Garuḍa-array fashioned by the son of Bharadvāja, Yudhiṣṭhira drew up his counter-formation in the shape of a half-circle.

sanskrit: mukham āsīt suparṇasya bhāradvājo mahārathaḥ śiro duryodhano rājā sodaryaiḥ sānugaiḥ saha
english: The mouth of the Garuḍa was the great chariot-warrior, the son of Bharadvāja; its head was King Duryodhana with his brothers and followers.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣī kṛtavarmā ca gautamaś cāsyatāṃ varaḥ bhūtavarmā kṣemaśarmā karakarṣaś ca vīryavān
english: Its two eyes were Kṛtavarman and the descendant of Gotama, the best of bowmen, together with Bhūtavarman, Kṣemaśarman, and the valiant Karakarṣa.

sanskrit: kaliṅgāḥ siṃhalāḥ prācyāḥ śūrābhīrā daśerakāḥ śakā yavanakāmbojās tathā haṃsapadāś ca ye
english: The Kaliṅgas, the Siṃhalas, the Easterners, the valiant Ābhīras, the Dāśerakas, the Śakas, the Yavanas, the Kāmbojas, and those who were the Haṃsapadas,

sanskrit: grīvāyāṃ śūrasenāś ca daradā madrakekayāḥ gajāśvarathapattyaughās tasthuḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: and the Śūrasenas, the Daradas, the Madras, and the Kekayas stood at the neck, a flood of elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers in their hundreds of thousands.

sanskrit: bhūriśravāḥ śalaḥ śalyaḥ somadattaś ca bāhlikaḥ akṣauhiṇyā vṛtā vīrā dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣam āśritāḥ
english: Bhūriśravas, Śala, Śalya, Somadatta, and Bāhlika, heroes encompassed by an akṣauhiṇī, took their stand upon the right wing.

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau kāmbojaś ca sudakṣiṇaḥ vāmaṃ pakṣaṃ samāśritya droṇaputrāgragāḥ sthitāḥ
english: Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, and Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja, taking their position on the left wing, stood with the son of Droṇa at their head.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhe kaliṅgāḥ sāmbaṣṭhā māgadhāḥ paundramadrakāḥ gāndhārāḥ śakuniprāgyāḥ pārvatīyā vasātayaḥ
english: At the back were the Kaliṅgas, the Ambaṣṭhas, the Māgadhas, the Pauṇḍras and Madrakas, the Gāndhāras led by Śakuni, the mountaineers, and the Vasātis.

sanskrit: pucche vaikartanaḥ karṇaḥ saputrajñātibāndhavaḥ mahatyā senayā tasthau nānādhvajasamutthayā
english: At the tail stood Karṇa, son of Vikartana, with his sons, kinsmen, and friends, attended by a mighty host that bristled with banners of every kind.

sanskrit: jayadratho bhīmarathaḥ sāṃyātrikasabho jayaḥ bhūmiṃjayo vṛṣakrātho naiṣadhaś ca mahābalaḥ
english: Jayadratha, Bhīmaratha, Sāṃyātrika, Sabhā, Jaya, Bhūmiṃjaya, Vṛṣakrātha, and the mighty Naiṣadha,

sanskrit: vṛtā balena mahatā brahmalokapuraskṛtāḥ vyūhasyopari te rājan sthitā yuddhaviśāradāḥ
english: surrounded by a great force and having the world of Brahmā as their goal, stood above the array, O king, those men skilled in war.

sanskrit: droṇena vihito vyūhaḥ padātyaśvarathadvipaiḥ vātoddhūtārṇavākāraḥ pravṛtta iva lakṣyate
english: The array marshalled by Droṇa, with its foot-soldiers, horses, chariots, and elephants, looked like the ocean lashed by the wind and surging into motion.

sanskrit: tasya pakṣaprapakṣebhyo niṣpatanti yuyutsavaḥ savidyutstanitā meghāḥ sarvadigbhya ivoṣṇage
english: From its wings and outer wings the eager combatants poured forth, like clouds charged with lightning and thunder from every quarter in the hot season.

sanskrit: tasya prāgjyotiṣo madhye vidhivat kalpitaṃ gajam āsthitaḥ śuśubhe rājann aṃśumān udaye yathā
english: In its midst the king of Prāgjyotiṣa, mounted upon an elephant duly caparisoned, shone, O king, like the radiant sun at its rising.

sanskrit: mālyadāmavatā rājā śvetacchatreṇa dhāryatā kṛttikāyogayuktena paurṇamāsyām ivendunā
english: The king, borne beneath a white parasol hung with wreaths and garlands, was like the full moon on the night of the full, in conjunction with the Kṛttikā stars.

sanskrit: nīlāñjanacayaprakhyo madāndho dvirado babhau abhivṛṣṭo mahāmeghair yathā syāt parvato mahān
english: That elephant, dark as a heap of black collyrium and blind with rut, gleamed like a great mountain rained upon by mighty clouds.

sanskrit: nānānṛpatibhir vīrair vividhāyudhabhūṣaṇaiḥ samanvitaḥ pārvatīyaiḥ śakro devagaṇair iva
english: Attended by sundry heroic kings of the mountains, adorned with weapons of every kind, he was like Śakra amid the hosts of the gods.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraḥ prekṣya vyūhaṃ tam atimānuṣam ajayyam aribhiḥ saṃkhye pārṣataṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, beholding that more-than-human array, unconquerable by foes in battle, spoke these words to the son of Pṛṣata:

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasya vaśaṃ nāham iyām adya yathā prabho pārāvatasavarṇāśva tathā nītir vidhīyatām
english: "O lord, master of horses gray as the dove, let such a plan be devised that I do not this day fall into the power of the Brāhmaṇa."

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumna uvāca droṇasya yatamānasya vaśaṃ naiṣyasi suvrata aham āvārayiṣyāmi droṇam adya sahānugam
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna said: "You shall not fall into the power of Droṇa, however he may strive, O true to your vows; this day I shall hold off Droṇa together with his followers.

sanskrit: mayi jīvati kauravya nodvegaṃ kartum arhasi na hi śakto raṇe droṇo vijetuṃ māṃ kathaṃ cana
english: While I live, O descendant of Kuru, you ought not to be troubled; for Droṇa is by no means able to vanquish me in battle."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam uktvā kiran bāṇān drupadasya suto balī pārāvatasavarṇāśvaḥ svayaṃ droṇam upādravat
english: Saṃjaya said: Having spoken thus and scattering arrows, the mighty son of Drupada, his horses gray as the dove, himself rushed against Droṇa.

sanskrit: aniṣṭadarśanaṃ dṛṣṭvā dhṛṣṭadyumnam avasthitam kṣaṇenaivābhavad droṇo nātihṛṣṭamanā iva
english: Seeing Dhṛṣṭadyumna planted before him, of unwelcome aspect, Droṇa in an instant became as one whose heart was not greatly cheered.

sanskrit: taṃ tu saṃprekṣya putras te durmukhaḥ śatrukarśanaḥ priyaṃ cikīrṣan droṇasya dhṛṣṭadyumnam avārayat
english: But beholding him, your son Durmukha, scourge of foes, wishing to do Droṇa a service, held off Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāras tumulaḥ samarūpa ivābhavat pārṣatasya ca śūrasya durmukhasya ca bhārata
english: That tumultuous clash between the heroic son of Pṛṣata and Durmukha, O Bhārata, seemed to be a contest of equals.

sanskrit: pārṣataḥ śarajālena kṣipraṃ pracchādya durmukham bhāradvājaṃ śaraugheṇa mahatā samavārayat
english: The son of Pṛṣata, swiftly veiling Durmukha with a net of arrows, beat back the son of Bharadvāja with a great flood of shafts.

sanskrit: droṇam āvāritaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhṛśāyastas tavātmajaḥ nānāliṅgaiḥ śaravrātaiḥ pārṣataṃ samamohayat
english: Seeing Droṇa held at bay, your son, sorely strained, bewildered the son of Pṛṣata with showers of arrows of every device.

sanskrit: tayor viṣaktayoḥ saṃkhye pāñcālyakurumukhyayoḥ droṇo yaudhiṣṭhiraṃ sainyaṃ bahudhā vyadhamac charaiḥ
english: While those two chiefs, the Pāñcāla and the Kuru, were locked together in the fray, Droṇa with his arrows scattered Yudhiṣṭhira's army in many directions.

sanskrit: anilena yathābhrāṇi vicchinnāni samantataḥ tathā pārthasya sainyāni vicchinnāni kva cit kva cit
english: As clouds are torn asunder on every side by the wind, so were Pārtha's forces torn apart, here and there.

sanskrit: muhūrtam iva tad yuddham āsīn madhuradarśanam tata unmattavad rājan nirmaryādam avartata
english: For a moment that battle was fair to behold; then, O king, it raged on as if frenzied, beyond all bounds.

sanskrit: naiva sve na pare rājann ajñāyanta parasparam anumānena saṃjñābhir yuddhaṃ tat samavartata
english: Neither one's own men nor the foe, O king, could any longer be told apart; that battle was waged by guesswork and by watchwords.

sanskrit: cūḍāmaṇiṣu niṣkeṣu bhūṣaṇeṣv asicarmasu teṣām ādityavarṇābhā marīcyaḥ pracakāśire
english: From their crest-jewels, their golden chains, their ornaments, their swords and shields, beams shone forth with the splendor of the sun.

sanskrit: tat prakīrṇapatākānāṃ rathavāraṇavājinām balākāśabalābhrābhaṃ dadṛśe rūpam āhave
english: The aspect of the chariots, elephants, and horses, with their banners scattered abroad, appeared in the battle like a sky dappled with cranes and clouds.

sanskrit: narān eva narā jaghnur udagrāś ca hayā hayān rathāṃś ca rathino jaghnur vāraṇā varavāraṇān
english: Men slew men, and fierce horses slew horses; charioteers slew charioteers, and elephants slew great elephants.

sanskrit: samucchritapatākānāṃ gajānāṃ paramadvipaiḥ kṣaṇena tumulo ghoraḥ saṃgrāmaḥ samavartata
english: Between elephants whose banners were upraised and other mighty elephants there arose in a moment a tumultuous and terrible combat.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ saṃsaktagātrāṇāṃ karṣatām itaretaram dantasaṃghātasaṃgharṣāt sadhūmo 'gnir ajāyata
english: From those beasts, their bodies locked together as they dragged at one another, fire mixed with smoke sprang up from the grinding clash of their tusks.

sanskrit: viprakīrṇapatākās te viṣāṇajanitāgnayaḥ babhūvuḥ khaṃ samāsādya savidyuta ivāmbudāḥ
english: With their banners scattered and fire kindled from their tusks, they became, as they reached toward the sky, like clouds charged with lightning.

sanskrit: vikṣaradbhir nadadbhiś ca nipatadbhiś ca vāraṇaiḥ saṃbabhūva mahī kīrṇā meghair dyaur iva śāradī
english: With the elephants—bleeding, trumpeting, and falling—the earth was strewn over, as the autumn sky is strewn with clouds.

sanskrit: teṣām āhanyamānānāṃ bāṇatomaravṛṣṭibhiḥ vāraṇānāṃ ravo jajñe meghānām iva saṃplave
english: From those elephants, smitten by the showers of arrows and lances, there arose a roar like the roar of clouds at the dissolution of the world.

sanskrit: tomarābhihatāḥ ke cid bāṇaiś ca paramadvipāḥ vitresuḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ śabdam evāpare 'vrajan
english: Some of the great elephants, struck by lances and by arrows, trembled in terror; others took to flight at the very din of every creature.

sanskrit: viṣāṇābhihatāś cāpi ke cit tatra gajā gajaiḥ cakrur ārtasvaraṃ ghoram utpātajaladā iva
english: And some elephants there, gored by the tusks of other elephants, raised a dreadful cry of anguish, like storm-clouds at a portent.

sanskrit: pratīpaṃ hriyamāṇāś ca vāraṇā varavāraṇaiḥ unmathya punar ājahruḥ preritāḥ paramāṅkuśaiḥ
english: And the elephants that were being driven backward by mighty elephants, urged on again by the keen goads, churned forward and returned to the charge.

sanskrit: mahāmātrā mahāmātrais tāḍitāḥ śaratomaraiḥ gajebhyaḥ pṛthivīṃ jagmur muktapraharaṇāṅkuśāḥ
english: The elephant-drivers, smitten by the arrows and lances of other drivers, let fall their weapons and goads and went down from the elephants to the ground.

sanskrit: nirmanuṣyāś ca mātaṅgā vinadantas tatas tataḥ chinnābhrāṇīva saṃpetuḥ saṃpraviśya parasparam
english: And the elephants, bereft of their men and trumpeting on every side, rushed together and crashed into one another like sundered clouds.
